documents.title: Exact keyword search
documents.text: Exact keyword search checks whether the query terms occur in each document. An inverted index makes this check fast. Direct term overlap gives a clear baseline, but it misses a relevant document when the document uses a synonym or a different phrase.

documents.title: BM25 ranking
documents.text: BM25 ranks lexical matches with term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. It rewards useful term overlap and reduces the effect of repeated common terms. BM25 cannot match a term to a synonym that is absent from the query or document.

documents.title: The inverted index
documents.text: An inverted index maps each term to a list of document IDs. A query can use the lists to find documents without scanning the full corpus. This data structure supports fast exact keyword search.

documents.title: Synonyms and paraphrases
documents.text: Paraphrase handling links automobile with car. It connects alternative expressions that describe one information need. A relevance decision checks whether two passages answer the same question.

documents.title: Dense embeddings
documents.text: A dense embedding maps each passage to a vector of numbers. The encoder captures patterns of meaning, so related passages can sit near each other even when their wording changes. This enables semantic retrieval.

documents.title: Vector similarity
documents.text: Cosine similarity compares a question vector with passage vectors. A high score signals a close representation. The measure can surface related phrasing, but it does not verify that a passage contains the required evidence.

documents.title: Chunking changes the search unit
documents.text: Chunking splits a long document into smaller passages. Small chunks can improve precision, while large chunks preserve context. The chunk size changes which text a retrieval method can rank.

documents.title: Metadata filters
documents.text: Metadata filters restrict the candidate set by fields such as date, author, or product. They can remove irrelevant documents before ranking. A filter cannot return information that the corpus does not contain.

documents.title: Reranking after retrieval
documents.text: Reranking reads the query and a first-stage candidate passage together. It can change the order of retrieved documents and improve the top results. It cannot rank a relevant document that candidate retrieval missed.

documents.title: Relevance labels
documents.text: A relevance label records whether a document satisfies a defined information need. A search score is not a relevance label. A person must define the label rule before evaluation.

documents.title: Retrieval evaluation
documents.text: Recall measures the share of relevant documents that a method retrieves. Mean reciprocal rank, or MRR, measures the position of the first relevant result. Each metric describes a different part of ranking quality.

documents.title: Missing and stale documents
documents.text: A missing document cannot appear in a result. A stale document can return old evidence. Corpus coverage and update policy limit every retrieval method, including exact search, BM25, and vector search.

main.text: How can a search system find relevant text when the user's words differ from the words in the documents?
main.purpose: The running query for the article. It asks for retrieval across different wording.

validation_direct.text: Which data structure maps terms to document IDs for fast exact keyword search?
validation_direct.purpose: A direct-term query. The relevant document contains the main query terms.

validation_paraphrase.text: How can a machine match a question to a passage that uses different language?
validation_paraphrase.purpose: A paraphrase query. It describes the semantic task without naming embeddings or cosine similarity.
